analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Publishing our 2027 Global Macro Outlooks
key_insights: Global equities rose 2.5% last week, led by Japan (+5.2%), EM (+3.2%) and Asia (+2.9%). Energy (+3.5%), Industrials (+3.4%) and Tech (+3.3%) led sector performance.
GS published its 2027 Global Macro Outlooks. The equity strategy outlook is titled 'Finding Value in Growth'.
2026 was the year of earnings. Equity returns were reasonable and similar across regions, strong earnings growth was the main driver, and all equity markets de-rated.

For 2027, GS expects earnings growth to slow, AI capex growth to peak, and the cost of capital to stay elevated. Investors are expected to seek companies that can sustain growth as it becomes scarcer.
GS forecasts positive equity returns in 2027 with higher volatility than in recent years.
GS equity themes for 2027: Growth, selective Defensives, and beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields.
On a risk-adjusted basis GS is overweight the US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, and underweight Europe.
GS 12-month targets: S&P 500 8700 (+15.1% from 7562), STOXX 600 700 (+5.4%), MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan 960 (+19.4%), Topix 4500 (+14.2%).
GS expects the US 10Y yield to fall from 5.2% to 4.7% in 12 months (-50bp), the German 10Y from 3.4% to 3.1%, and the Japan 10Y from 2.9% to 2.8%.
GS expects Brent to fall from $95.8 to $81 in 12 months (-15.3%), gold to rise from $3878 to $4570 (+17.8%), and LME copper from $13468 to $15580 (+15.7%).
GS FX forecasts at 12 months: EUR/USD 1.15 from 1.10, GBP/USD 1.34 from 1.32, USD/JPY 150 from 160.
Consensus EPS growth for 2027: S&P 500 16.5% (from 32.4% in 2026), STOXX 600 8.4% (from 23.9%), TOPIX 13.9% (from 21.3%), MSCI AP ex Japan 30.2% (from 77.0%), MSCI AC World 17.0% (from 35.7%).
Consensus 2027 sector EPS growth is led by IT (+44.8%). Energy (-11.0%) and Communication Services (-4.8%) are expected to decline.
The GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator stands at 67%, with Shiller PE at 39.3 (97th percentile) and unemployment at 4.1 (82nd percentile on GS's inverted scale).
Momentum remained volatile after a sharp recent unwind, and 2026 equity fund inflows moved above previous years.
Week-ahead data: US retail sales and many Fed speakers; UK October CPI and labour data; Japan Q3 GDP and October core CPI; China October activity; Shenzhen APEC Summit.
